The supreme Goddess, who effects the creation, destruction, and preservation of the universe, should be meditated upon with her lotus-hands raised, holding the finest grain, her own tusk, and a jewel-pitcher; likewise, she holds a book, a full pitcher, the *vilasat* mudrā, and a rosary. The Lord, beginning from his upper right hand, holds the citron and other attributes; below—

The Goddess holds a book and other objects beginning with her left hand. *Oṃ aṃ gaṃ namaḥ*, *oṃ āṃ gaṃ namaḥ*, and so forth is the sequence of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). One should perform the placement in this manner during the worship of Gaṇapati. Now, for the sake of attaining sovereignty, [the mantra] begins with the seed-syllable of Śakti. Śakti is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Sarasvatī, the mother of the universe, is the deity (*devatā*).

The application for the sake of all sovereignty is as follows: *hrāṃ hrīṃ* and so forth is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The meditation (*dhyāna*): She possesses a beautiful form rivaling ten million rising suns; her breasts are firm; she is adorned with a crescent moon on her crown, necklaces, a girdle, and anklets; and she holds in her lotus-like hands a rosary, a noose, a goad, and a book.

May the three-eyed Jagadīśvarī, holding a lotus, bestow prosperity upon you. Beginning from the lower right hand, one should meditate on the rosary and so forth. *Aṃ hrīṃ namaḥ*, *Āṃ hrīṃ namaḥ*, and so forth is the sequence for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
Worship and other rites are as before; this is appropriate for the propitiation of Durgā. Now, Śrī...

43a) For the sake of attainment, the placement (*nyāsa*) of the seed-syllable of Śrī: Bhṛgu is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), Mātṛkā in the form of Śrī is the deity (*devatā*); the application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of the increase of prosperity during the placement of Mātṛkā. Oṃ aṃ śrī namaḥ.

Oṃ Āṃ Śrī Namaḥ. [And so forth. Meditation: One should meditate upon her, whose radiance is like a flash of lightning, being sprinkled with the nectar of immortality drawn up by the trunks of four elephants resembling the snowy mountains; she holds in her lotus-like hands a rosary, two lotuses, and a book.

One should meditate upon the Mistress of the Universe, resplendent with a brilliant golden luster and possessing a slightly contracted form. Beginning from the lower right hand, four objects—the rosary (*japapaṭī*) and so forth—are to be meditated upon. Thus one should place [the mantras] for the propitiation of Lakṣmī.
Now, for the purpose of subjugation (*vaśya*), [the mantra] begins with the *Kāma-bīja*. Sammohana is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Paṅkti is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Kāmajananī is the deity.

The deity is Sarasvatī; the application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of subjugation in the Mātṛkā-nyāsa. The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) are *klāṃ klīṃ*, and so forth. As for the visualization (dhyāna): [I meditate upon her] who is as radiant as ten million rising suns, holding a crystal rosary, a bow, and the five arrows of Smara, and bearing the Vidyā.
One should meditate upon the Mother of all beings, who holds lotuses in her hands, possesses three eyes, and has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament.
On the right hand, place a rosary and a book; above those, the five arrows and the bow.
The worship and other rites are as before. Perform the *nyāsa* as follows: *Aṃ klīṃ namaḥ*, *Āṃ klīṃ namaḥ*, and so forth.
This is for the purpose of subjugation (*vaśya*). Now, the *nyāsa* for the sake of subjugating Lakṣmī, the Goddess of Sovereignty: Brahmā is the *ṛṣi*, Gāyatrī [is the meter]...
The meter is Triśaktirūpiṇī; the enchantress Sarasvatī is the deity; the application is for the purpose of sovereignty in the ritual placement (nyāsa).
With the three seed-syllables *hrīṃ*, *śrīṃ*, and *klīṃ* in both direct and reverse order, one performs the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*).
I meditate upon her holding a rosary, a noose, arrows, and a goad; two lotuses, a goad, arrows, and nine books.
She who manifests herself with her own hands, who is distressed by the red mark on her breast, the enchantress with three eyes and the young moon as her crest-ornament.

In the two upper left hands are two lotuses; below those, a noose and a goad; below those, an arrow and a bow; and below those, a rosary and a book. The worship and other rites are as before. *Oṃ aṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namaḥ*. *Āṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namaḥ*. Such is the sequence of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Now:

The Śrīkaṇṭhādi-nyāsa is recommended for the worship of Śiva. Dakṣimūrti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), and Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (devatā). Its application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of all human goals (puruṣārtha) preceded by the Śrīkaṇṭhādi-nyāsa. The six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) ritual begins with *hlāṃ hlīṃ* and so forth. There is also a meditation (dhyāna):

I take refuge in the Lord who resembles the Bandhūka flower and gold, who holds a beautiful rosary, a noose, a goad, and the gesture of granting boons with his own staff-like arms; who wears the crescent moon as an ornament, has three eyes, and possesses a half-moon on his forehead, resembling the night with its disheveled hair. [The attributes are held] starting from the lower right hand: the rosary and so forth. Oṃ Aṃ.
Salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha and Pūrṇodarī (1); Āṃ, to Ananteśa and Virajā (2); Iṃ, to Sūkṣma and Śālmali (3); Īṃ, to Trimūrti and Lolākṣī (4); Oṃ, to Amareśvara and Vartulākṣī (5);
Oṃ, to Arcīśa and Dīrghaghoṇā (6); Ṛṃ, to Bhārabhūti and Sudīrghamukhī (7); Ṝṃ, to Atithīśa...
To Gomukhya, ḷṃ; to Sthāṇvīśa and Dīrghajihvā, ḹṃ; to Hara and Kuṇḍodarī, 8;
to Jhaṇṭīśa and Ūrdhvakeśinī, eṃ; to Bhautikeśa and Vikṛtamukhī, aiṃ; to Sadyojāta and Jvālāmukhī, oṃ; to Anugraheśa and Ulkāmukhī, 14; to Akrūreśa, aṃ.
To Śrīmukhya, 15; to Krodhīśa and Mahākālī, 17; to Khaṃ Caṇḍīśa and Sarasvatī, 18;
to Gaṃ Pañcānta and Sarvasiddhi, 19; to Ghaṃ Śivottama and Gaurī, 20; to Ṅaṃ Ekarudreśa and Trailokyavidyā, 21; to Caṃ Kūrmeśa and Mantraśakti, 22; to Chaṃ...
To Ekanetrā, the power of the Self (ātmaśakti), svāhā! To Caturānanā, the mother of Īśāna, svāhā! To Ajeśā, the mother of Lāṅgulin, svāhā! 23–25.

ṆAṂ to Sarveśāyadrāviṇī 26; ṬAṂ to Someśāyanāgarī 27; ṬHAṂ to Lāṅgalīśakhacarī 28; ḌAṂ to Dārukeśamañjarī 29; ḌHAṂ to Ardhanārīśvararūpiṇī 30; ṆAṂ to Umākānteśavīriṇī 31; TAṂ to Āvyāniśakoṭarī 32; THAṂ to Daṇḍīśa...
*Pūtanāyai* 33 *daṃ*, to Atrīśa and Bhadrayoginī; 34 *dhaṃ*, to Mīneśa and Śaṅkhinī; 35 *naṃ*, to Meṣeśa and Garjinī; 36 *paṃ*, to Lohiteśa and Kālarātri; 37 *phaṃ*, to Śikhīśa and Kurdinī;
38 *vaṃ*, to Chagaleśa and Kapardinī; 39 *bhaṃ*, to Dviraṇḍeśa and Vajrā; 40 *maṃ*.

To Mahākāla, for Jāyā (41); *yaṃ* to the self of the skin, to Kapālīśa, for Sumukheśvarī (42); *raṃ* to the self of the blood, to Bhujaṅgeśa, for Revatī (43); *laṃ* to the self of the flesh, to Pinākīśa, for Mādhavī (44);
*vaṃ* to the self of the fat, to Khaḍgīśa, for Vāruṇī (45); *śaṃ* to the self of the bone, to Vakreśa.

Vāyavyai 46, *ṣaṃ* to Majjātman Śveteśa and Rakṣyā Vadhāriṇī 47; *saṃ* to Śukrātman Bhṛgvīśa and Sahajā 48; *haṃ* to Lakulīśa and Mahālakṣmī 49; *laṃ* to Śiveśa and Vyāpinī 50; *kṣaṃ* to Saṃvartakeśa and Māyā 50—*namaḥ*, [thus] in the previously mentioned locations.

The sequence of placement (*nyāsakrama*): worship and so forth are as in the *Mātṛkā*. Now, for the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, there is the placement (*nyāsa*) of Keśava and others, preceded by the *Kāmabīja* (the seed-syllable of desire). Prajāpati is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), and Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the deity (*devatā*). The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining the fourfold aims of human life through this placement. *klāṃ klīṃ*.

The six-limbed [mantra] and meditation: May the body of Puṇḍarīkākṣa (Viṣṇu) and Lakṣmī protect you—a body that has become one through their close embrace, with his left hand resting upon her high breast, appearing as if inseparable due to the lack of space between them; he who holds in his hands the lotus, mace, conch, and discus, as well as the Vidyā, the lotus-mirror, and the golden pitcher, and who possesses the splendor of lightning amidst clouds.
44b) Beginning from the lower right hand, there are the lotus and so forth;
in the portion belonging to Lakṣmī, beginning from the lower left hand, there are the vidyā and so forth.

*klīṃ* *aṃ* obeisance to Keśava and Kīrti; *klīṃ* *āṃ* obeisance to Nārāyaṇa and Kānti; *iṃ* obeisance to Mādhava and Tuṣṭi; *īṃ* obeisance to Govinda and Puṣṭi; *uṃ* obeisance to Viṣṇu and Dhṛti; *ūṃ* obeisance to Madhusūdana and Kānti; *oṃ* obeisance to Trivikrama and Kriyā; *oṃ* obeisance to Vāmana and Dayā; *ḷṃ*...
To Śrīdhara and Medhā; to Hṛṣīkeśa and Harṣā; to Padmanābha and Śraddhā;
to Dāmodara and Lajjā; to Vāsudeva and Lakṣmī;
to Saṃkarṣaṇa and Sarasvatī; to Pradyumna and Prīti; to Aniruddha and Rati.

Kaṃ to Kañcakrin, Jayā; khaṃ to Khadgin, Durgā; gaṃ to Śārṅgin, Prabhā; ghaṃ to Khaḍgin, Satyā; ṅaṃ to Śaṅkhin, Caṇḍā; caṃ to Halin, Vāṇī; chaṃ to Muśalin, Vilāsinī; jaṃ to Śūlin, Vijayā; jhaṃ to Pāśin, Virajā; ñaṃ...
Aṃ to Aṅkuśin, Viśvā; Ṭaṃ to Mukunda, Viśadā; Ṭhaṃ to Nandaja, Sunandā;
Oṃ to Nandin, Smṛti; Ḍhaṃ to Nārāyaṇa, Ṛddhi; Ṇaṃ to Narakañjit, Samṛddhi; Taṃ to Hari, Śuddhi; Thaṃ to Kṛṣṇa, Bhukti; Daṃ to Satya.
To Śuddhi—*dhaṃ* to Sātvanāyamatya; *naṃ* to Śauri and Kṣamā; *paṃ* to Śūra and Ramā;
*phaṃ* to Janārdana and Umā; *vaṃ* to Bhūdharā and Kledinī; *bhaṃ* to Viśvamūrti and Klinnā; *maṃ* to Vaikuṇṭha and Vasudhā; *yaṃ* to Puruṣottama and Vasudhā; *raṃ*.
Valineparāyai; Laṃ to Valānujāyaparāyai; Vaṃ to Valāyapārāyaṇāyai; Śaṃ to Vṛṣaghnāya-saṃdhyāyai; Ṣaṃ to Vṛṣāya-prajñāyai; Saṃ to Hasāya-prabhāyai. (45a)

One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) in the previously mentioned locations with: *haṃ* to Varāha and Niśā; *laṃ* to Vimala and Amoghā; and *kṣaṃ* to Nṛsiṃha and Vidyutā, followed by *namaḥ*. Worship and other rites are as before. Now follows the placement of the Kalās of the Praṇava:
Prajāpati is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and Sarasvatī, whose nature consists of the Kalās, is the deity (*devatā*).

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of liberation. *Aṃ ūṃ āṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *iṃ uṃ īṃ* to the head, *svāhā*; *uṃ ūṃ oṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*. Thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Meditation (*dhyāna*): [He holds] in his hands a lotus, a discus, a bowstring, a deer, a book, a rosary, and a bright chisel.
I bow to Śāradā, who bears a skull-cup and a leaf as well as a shining golden jar of nectar; who is adorned with pearls and lightning-like [ornaments];
who has five faces, each with three eyes, and is beautiful with fresh *japā* flowers; who is bent by the weight of her breasts;
and who resembles the full moon. Or, beginning from the lower left hand...

Having meditated thus upon the lotuses and so forth, one should install the entire *mātṛkā*. It is as follows: Oṃ Aṃ to Nivṛtti; Āṃ to Pratiṣṭhā; Iṃ to Vidyā; Īṃ to Śānti; Uṃ to Īndhikā; Ūṃ to Dīpikā; Ṛṃ to Recikā; Ṝṃ to Mocikā; Ḷṃ to Sūkṣmā; Ḹṃ to Sūkṣmāmṛtā; Eṃ...

To Jñānā; aiṃ to Jñānāmṛtā; oṃ to Āpyāyinī; oṃ to Vyāpinī; aṃ to Vyomarūpā; aḥ to Anantā; kaṃ to Sṛṣṭi; khaṃ to Ṛddhi; gaṃ to Smṛti; ghaṃ to Medhā; ṅaṃ to Kānti; caṃ to Lakṣmī; chaṃ to Dūtī; jaṃ to Sthirā; jhaṃ.

To Sthiti; to Jñā for accomplishment; to Ṭaṃ for old age; to Ṭhaṃ for Mālinī; to Ḍaṃ for Peace (Śānti); to Ḍhaṃ for Sovereignty (Aiśvaryā); to Ṇaṃ for Delight (Rati); to Taṃ for Kāminī; to Thaṃ for the Giver of Boons (Varadā); to Daṃ for Refreshment (Hlādinī); to Dhaṃ for Affection (Prīti);
to Naṃ for the Long One (Dīrghā); to Paṃ for the Sharp One (Tīkṣṇā); to Phaṃ for the Fierce One (Raudrā); to Baṃ for Fear (Bhayā); to Bhaṃ for Sleep (Nidrā).
The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is performed in the aforementioned locations with the following: *maṃ* to Tandrī; *yaṃ* to Kṣudhā; *raṃ* to Krodhinī; *laṃ* to Kriyā; *vaṃ* to Utkārī;
*śaṃ* to Mṛtyu; *ṣaṃ* to Prītā; *saṃ* to Śvetā; *haṃ* to Aruṇā; *laṃ* to Amitā; and *kṣaṃ* to Anantā—*namaḥ*. Thus is the placement declared.
45b) The worship and so forth are as before.

Now follows the placement (nyāsa) for the sacrifice of manifestation (prapañcayāga): Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), Yaṃ Tejorūpiṇī Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā); its application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of all things through this placement. Svāhā, salutation to the heart (hṛdaya).
1 So'haṃ, svāhā to the head (śiras). 2 Haṃsaḥ, vaṣaṭ to the tuft (śikhā). 3 Hrīṃ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca). 4 Oṃ.

*vauṣaṭ* to the three eyes; *phaṭ* to the weapon of Hari-Hara—thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The Meditation (*Dhyāna*): I worship that supreme splendor, which is like a deep ocean of nectar—the single root of the universe, incessantly measured by the five mantras beginning with *Tāra* (Om), immeasurable by worldly standards, the very essence of consciousness, the primordial sound (*svara*) of all speech, and the imperishable.

Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā—on the face (1). Oṃ hrīṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā—on the right arm (2). Oṃ hrīṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā—[on the left arm] (3).
On the left arm: 3 Oṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā.
On the right foot: 4 Oṃ hrīṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ haṃ saḥ sohaṃ svāhā.
On the left foot: 5 Oṃ hrīṃ paṃ phaṃ vaṃ bhaṃ maṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā. On the head: 6 Oṃ.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on the chest with: *hrīṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā* (7), the eight-syllable mantra of the Supreme Self— *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā*— should be recited by those seeking liberation even without its connection to the *mātṛkā*.

As for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *oṃ hrīṃ aṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā*; *oṃ hrīṃ āṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā*. In this manner, the placement is performed in the previously mentioned locations. By such placement, one becomes possessed of a divine body. Now follows the placement of the planets (*grahanyāsa*).

Aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ, salutation to Āditya in the face. (1) Kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ, salutation to Aṅgāraka on the right arm. (2) Caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ, salutation to Śukra on the left arm. (3)
46a) Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Budha on the right foot; 4 taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ, obeisance to Bṛhaspati on the left foot; 5 paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ, [obeisance] to Śanaiścara.

*Namaḥ* to the belly (6): *yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ*. *Namaḥ* to Soma on the chest (7). Now, for the sake of great prosperity (*mahāsampad*), follows the *nyāsa* known as the "Fulfiller of the Lotus of Power" (*śaktikamalāpūraka*). The *nyāsa* begins with: *aṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*, *āṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ*, and so forth. This is according to the specific divisions found in the *Kānanavṛtta* and other texts.

Now follows the placement (nyāsa) for the accomplishment of everything: *aṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ drāṃ klīṃ hlūṃ saḥ*, and so forth. Thus, this is the placement with the bindu (*bindukanyāsa*) and the placement of the digits (*kalānyāsa*). The placement of the planets (*grahanyāsa*) and the placement of the sacrifice of the universe (*prapañcayāganyāsa*) are praised in all tantras. We shall also know other placements of the Mātṛkās; those...
We do not write [further] for fear of excessive length of the book. Thus ends the eighth chapter, concerning the Mātṛkā-nyāsa, in the *Mantrakoṣa* compiled by the venerable Āsāditya Tripāṭhī.
Now follow the Sārasvata mantras.

Therein is the *bhūtalipi* (earth-script): a, i, u, ū, ḷ, e, ai, o, au, ha, ya, ra, va, la; 3. iṃ, ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa; ca, cha, ja, jha, ña; 5. ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa; ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa; 6. ta, tha, da, dha, na; ta, tha, da, dha, na; 7. pa, pha, ba, bha, ma; pa, pha, ba, bha, ma; 8. ya, ra, la, va, śa; ya, ra, la, va, śa; 9. ṣa, sa, ha, kṣa. Thus are the nine groups (*navavarga*). Having extracted one letter from each of these, the five groups beginning with space (*vyomādi*) are to be formed.

Namely: *a e ha ṅa ña ṇa na ma śāḥ*—this is the group of space (1); *ī ai ya ka va da ta paṃ ṣāḥ*—this is the group of wind (2); *uṃ ūṃ ra kha cha ṭha tha pha ṇaḥ*—this is the group of fire (3); *oṃ auṃ va gha ṛ ḍha dha ma*—this is the group of water (4); *ḷ ṝ ḷ ga ja ḍa da vā*—this is the group of earth (5). Thus.

The Bhūtalipi mantra consists of forty-two syllables. Dakṣiṇāmūrti is its seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is its meter (chandas), Varṇeśvarī is its deity (devatā), and it is employed for the purpose of acquiring knowledge (vidyārtha). The six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) are formed by the six groups of consonants beginning with 'ha'. [The following is] the meditation (dhyāna):
46b) She who resembles ten million moons freed from the dark spot, with full and lofty breasts, her head marked by the crescent moon,
her three eyes rolling from the intoxication of honey-wine, and bearing a rosary of beads and a yellow garment— Japapati.
I take refuge in Vāgīśvarī, the primordial knowledge, who holds a skull-bowl and a lotus, whose body is inscribed with letters, and who rivals the beauty of youth;

[her hands] beginning from the lower right hand hold the gestures of boon-granting (*vara*) and so forth. Having thus meditated and having invoked the Goddess upon the previously mentioned pedestal, one should worship her. Now follows the ten-syllable mantra of Vāgvādinī: *vadavada vāgvādini svāhā*. Of this...

The sage is Kāśyapa, the metre is Virāj, the deity is Vāgvādinī, and the application is for the purpose of knowledge. *Vaṃ* is the seed-syllable; *svāhā* is the emblem. One should assign the power (*śakti*) to the feet and the womb. *Vāk* is the bolt. Having performed the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) as taught in the Mātṛkā-vidhi—beginning with *aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*, and so forth—one should [assign] the syllables of the mantra.
One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): *vaṃ* on the head; *daṃ* on the right ear (2); *vaṃ* on the left ear (3); *daṃ* on the right eye (4);
*vāṃ* on the left eye (5); *vāṃ* on the right nostril (6); *diṃ* on the left nostril (7); *niṃ* on the mouth (8); *svaṃ* on the sixth [limb];
*īṃ* and *hāṃ* on the forehead (*yude*). The meditation (*dhyāna*): [She is] seated upon a stainless lotus, holding a writing brush.

May the sister Bhāratī protect us from the fears of worldly existence— she whose pair of hands raised in the gesture of holding a book is adorned with a crest-jewel that shines like a fragment of the moon, surpassing the jasmine,
mandāra, and mandāra flowers. [Visualizing her] with a sword in the right hand and a book in the left, one should meditate upon her on the lotus seat as described for the Mothers.

Having worshipped the pedestal powers (pīṭha-śaktis) on the petals starting from the east and in the center with "Salutation to Medhā," "Salutation to Prajñā," "Salutation to Prabhā," "Salutation to Vidyā," "Salutation to Dhī," "Salutation to Dhṛti," "Salutation to Smṛti," and "Salutation to Vidyeśvarī," and having consecrated the pedestal in its pericarp with "Salutation to the Lotus-Seated One who possesses all powers," one should invoke the Goddess.

One should perform worship. Having recited the root mantra, one should offer: "This is the water for the feet (pādya); this is the water for the feet (arghya); this is the water for sipping (ācamanīya); [this is] the second sipping; [this is] the sipping for the garment"; and one should present three handfuls of flowers along with unbroken rice grains (akṣata) and kuśa grass.
Then follows the worship of the limbs (*aṅga-āvaraṇa*). One should worship the six limbs in the directions of Agni, Īśa, Asura, and Vāyu, as well as in front and behind.

Then, on the petals of the lotus, one should worship in order starting from the east with: "Obeisance to Yogā" (1), "to Satyā" (2), "to Vimalā" (3), "to Jñānā" (4), "to Smṛti" (5), "to Buddhi" (6), "to Medhā" (7), and "obeisance to Prajñā" (8).

One should worship with: "Obeisance to Brāhmī 1, Māheśvarī 2, Kaumārī 3, Vaiṣṇavī 4, Vārāhī 5, Māhendrī 6, Cāmuṇḍā 7, and Mahālakṣmī 8. Then: "Obeisance to Indra, the lord of the gods, together with his weapons and his vehicle 1; obeisance to Agni, the lord of splendor 2; obeisance to Yama, the lord of the departed spirits 3."
To Nirṛti, Lord of the Rākṣasas (4); to Varuṇa, Lord of the Waters (5); to Vāyu, Lord of the Vital Breath (6); to Kuvera, Lord of the Yakṣas (7);
to Īśāna, Lord of the Mountains (8); between Nirṛti and Varuṇa, to Ananta, Lord of the Nāgas (9);
between Īśāna and Indra, to Brahmā, Lord of the World (10)—[to each] together with his weapons and...

One should worship with "Salutation to Vāhanā" in one's own directions. Having worshipped thus and recited the mantra according to one's capacity, one should offer the recitation with the words, "May Vāgvādinī be pleased by this recitation. Then, having bowed and offered praise, one should dismiss her with the *saṃhāra-mudrā*.

The preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) consists of one million recitations. The fire oblation (homa) should be performed with ten thousand white lotuses smeared with milk, or with sesame seeds smeared with the three sweets (trimadhu).
Having drunk that consecrated water, one should recite the mantra a thousand times every day;
within a year, one will undoubtedly become a great poet and a master of counsel.
One should offer oblations with flowers produced from the rājavṛkṣa tree that are saturated with honey, and with its fuel-sticks; thereby one shall obtain incomparable poetic skill.
Now follows the sixteen-syllable Vāgvādinī mantra: *Aiṃ namo bhagavati vadavadavāgdevi svāhā*.
The seer (*ṛṣi*) and other [constituent elements] are as previously stated.

Aiṃ is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Svāhā is the power (*śakti*), and Vāk is the pin (*kīlaka*); this is the application (*viniyoga*) for the attainment of speech. Aiṃ, salutation to the heart (1). Namaḥ, Svāhā to the head (2). Bhagavati, Vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*) (3). Vadavada, Huṃ to the armor (*kavaca*) (4). Vāgdevi, Vauṣaṭ to the three eyes (5). Svāhā, Phaṭ to the weapon (*astra*) (6). The visualization (*dhyāna*): [She is] white...

I bow to the goddess of speech, who has three eyes, who bestows the power of eloquence, who sits upon a lotus, whose lotus-hands hold a crystal rosary, a garland, a garment, a cool moon-disc, a blazing book, a string of beads, a jar full of nectar, and a lotus, and who is graced with a beautiful smile and breasts that are slightly bent.

[She is] the bestower of the wealth of good fortune. Beginning from the lower right hand, she bears the four [attributes] such as the book (vyākhyā) and so forth. The worship and other rites are as previously described. Now follows the mantra of Haṃsavāgīśvarī, the fully manifested Sarasvatī:
*oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ*. [This is] the mantra of Haṃsavāgīśvarī.

Śakti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the metre (chandas), Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā); the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of speech. Hraiṃ, salutation to the heart, and so forth, constitutes the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga). Or, with "Aiṃ, salutation" and so forth, one should place the mantra-syllables upon the aperture of Brahmā, the center of the eyebrows, the eyes, the two ears, the two nostrils, the tongue, the penis, and the anus.

One should perform the placement (vinyāsa). Then follows the meditation (dhyāna): [I meditate upon] Vāṇī, who is like the full moon, whose face is radiant, and who possesses the luster of camphor and the *kunda* flower; her head is marked by the crescent moon, and she respectfully holds in her own hands a lute, a rosary, a jar filled with nectar, and the [divine] knowledge (*vidyā*).
I worship her who has four breasts, whose body is adorned with divine ornaments, and who is mounted upon a swan.

One should meditate on her holding a lute in her lower right hand and the Vidyā (scriptural knowledge) in her lower left hand, while holding a rosary and a jar of nectar with her two upper hands. Then, having performed the mental worship:
Having performed the external worship along with *medhā* and the others, one should invoke and worship the Goddess on the *pīṭha* as described by the Mothers.
(48a) With the limbs [of the mantra], there is the first enclosure; to the right and left sides of the Goddess, [one offers] "Salutation to Saṃskṛtā."

Salutation to Prākṛtā. Then, one should worship on the petals with: "Salutation to Prajñā, Medhā, Śruti, Śakti, Smṛti, Vāgīśvarī, Sumati, and Svasti. On those very [petals], one should worship the powers (śaktis) beginning with Brāhmī.
One should also worship the world-protectors (lokapālas) in the directions. The preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) consists of twelve hundred thousand [repetitions].

The *homa* sacrifice is performed with white lotuses using a tenth part [of the total count]. Now follows the *vākpati* mantra: *Aiṃ vācaspate amṛtepluvaḥ pluḥ*. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) and other attributes are as previously stated. *Aiṃ vācaspate amṛte pluvaḥ pluḥ*. With these, the five limbs [are assigned], excluding the eyes. The visualization (*dhyāna*): Seated upon a lotus, [holding] a rosary in her hands...

Holding two lotuses and a book, wearing a crown bound with the young moon, possessing the luster of a pearl, jasmine, and the moon, her eyes blossoming from her brow, weary from the weight of her breasts, and constantly attended by hosts of sages— may that Goddess of Speech grant you prosperity. (The left and right [hands] are above.)

In her two hands are two lotuses; in her lower hands are a rosary and a book. Having meditated thus, one should invoke the Goddess upon the previously mentioned pedestal and worship her. The preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of eleven hundred thousand recitations, and the fire-oblation (*homa*) is performed with clarified butter in ten parts of that number.
Having recited this vidyā, one should eat the leaf of the Brāhmī plant;
thus the wise person does not forget the Vedas and Āgamas once they have been heard.

Having recited [the mantra] five times over the paste of *brāhmī* juice and the like, along with *kapilā* ghee, one should drink it at the beginning of each day; by doing so daily, one becomes a knower of the meaning of all scriptures.
Now follows the three-syllabled mantra of Sarasvatī: *vāṃ rūṃ svoṃ*. It has no seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth.
The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) are formed by repeating the three seed-syllables twice. The visualization (*dhyāna*) is as follows:

I bow for a long time to the Sovereign of Speech, who is white like a pearl necklace, adorned with a crescent moon upon her head, and who bears in her own arms the gestures of exposition, a rosary, a jeweled vase, and a book; she whose waist bends under the weight of her full and lofty breasts, the mistress of the three worlds.

Having meditated upon Vinatā seated upon a lotus, with a book and a rosary in her two right hands, and a water-pot and a manuscript in her two left hands—one should worship her according to the ritual procedure for the worship of Mātṛkā. The preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of three hundred thousand recitations; the fire-oblation (*homa*) is performed ten times the number of recitations using milk-rice (*pāyasa*) consecrated with *āḍhya* [clarified butter].
A practitioner who recites the three seed-syllables of Japan shall attain victory in the assembly;
having recited white vacā or brāhmī, one should consume it at the break of day.
The practitioner obtains wisdom or his desired objects; there is no doubt in this matter.

Now, the mantra of Saptakoṭīśvarī: *Kaḥ saḥ Caṇḍikeśaḥ kaḥ*. Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chaṃdaḥ*), Saptakoṭīśvarī is the deity (*devatā*), *kaṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *saḥ* is the power (*śakti*), and *caṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of knowledge (*vidyā*). The six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) is performed with *Sāṃ Sīṃ*, and so forth. Worship and other rites are like those of Tripurā. Now, Vāgvādinī.

The Mālā-mantra consists of thirty syllables: *oṃ vadavada vāgvādini hrīṃ klīṃ klinne kledini mahākṣobhaṃ kuru sauḥ mokṣaṃ kuruṣva oṃ*. The Ṛṣi and other [limbs] are the same as those for Vāgīśvarī. Now, the Tripurabhairavī mantra: *hrauṃ hklīṃ hrauṃ*.

Śakti is the Ṛṣi, Gāyatrī is the metre, Tripurabhairavī is the deity; the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of knowledge and other perfections. The first syllable is the seed (bīja), the final syllable is the power (śakti), and the letter *ra* is the pin (kīlaka). Hraiṃ, salutation to the heart (1); Hraiṃ, svāhā to the head (2); Hraiṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā) (3); Hraiṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes (4); Hraiṃ...
*Kavacāya hūṃ* (five times), *Hraiṃ astrāya phaṭ* (six times). 49a) *Hrāṃ hrīṃ*, etc., are the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the *Śāradā*. *Aiṃdrāṃ drāvaṇavāṇāya namaḥ* (1).

Aiṃ Aindrī, salutation to the arrow of enchantment (2); Aiṃ Klīṃ, salutation to the arrow of inflaming (3); Aiṃ Klūṃ, salutation to the arrow of tormenting (4); Aiṃ Saḥ, salutation to the arrow of subjugation (5). One should thus place [these mantras] upon the foundation, the navel, the heart, the face, and the head. Aiṃ, salutation to the God of Love who enchants (1); Aiṃ Klīṃ...
*Aiṃ klīṃ klūṃ* to Kaṃdarpakāma; *aiṃ strīṃ* to Makaradhvajakāma;
*aiṃ strīṃ* to Manmathakāma—thus [the nyāsa] is performed upon these very [limbs]. Many such nyāsas have not been written here for fear of making the text too voluminous.
The visualization (*dhyāna*): [He is] possessing the splendor of a thousand rising suns, wearing a crimson silken garment, and a garland of heads upon his head.

I bow to the Goddess who wears a crown of jewels and the crescent moon, whose face is graced with a gentle smile, and who possesses the beauty of a three-eyed lotus-face; she holds a red-stained lotus, a rosary, a book, the gesture of fearlessness, and the boon-granting mudrā in her lotus-hands. In her upper right and left hands, she holds a rosary and a book.
Having meditated thus on the gestures of fearlessness (*abhaya*) and boon-granting (*vara*) in the lower right and left [hands], and after performing the mental worship (*mānasikapūjā*),
one should draw the wheel of the nine triangles (*navayonicakra*) within the twelve-petaled lotus upon the *śaktipīṭha* starting from the *ādhāra*; then, on the lotus petals,
[one worships] Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā (2), Raudrī (3), Ambikā (4), Icchā (5), Jñānā (6), and Satkṛtā.

One should worship with the mantra: "Obeisance to Kubjikā (7), Pradvī (8), Viṣaghnī (9), Dūtī (10), Bhūtī (11), and Sarvānandā (12). In the Śāradā-tilaka, however, there is an eight-petaled lotus; there, these powers (śaktis) are to be worshipped:
Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Kāminī, Kāmadāyinī, Rati, Ratipriyā, Ānandā, and Manonmanī.

In the center: Then, in the middle of the nine-yoni diagram, having worshipped the seat with the mantra "Aiṃ, obeisance to Parā (1), Aparā (2), and Parāparā (3); obeisance to Hasauḥ Sadāśiva Mahāpreta Padmāsana," one should invoke the Goddess there and worship her.

49b) Then follows the limb-worship (*aṅgapūjā*). Then, having worshipped four arrows in the primary directions starting from the east within the hexagon—both in the middle and on the outside—one should worship the fifth arrow in the space in front of the Goddess with: *drāṃ śoṣaṇavāṇāya*.

One should worship as follows: *namaḥ* (1), *drīṃ* to the Enchanting Arrow, *namaḥ* (2), *klīṃ* to the Inflaming Arrow, *namaḥ* (3), *klūṃ* to the Heating Arrow, *namaḥ* (4), *saḥ* to the Intoxicating Arrow, *namaḥ* (5). Then, in the center of the Yoni and in the remaining Yonis, starting from the east in sequence, one should worship: *subhagāyai* (1), *bhagāyai* (2), *bhagasarpiṇyai* (3).

One should worship with: "Salutation to Bhagamālinī" (4), "to Anaṅgā" (5), "to Anaṅgakusumā" (6), "to Anaṅgamekhalā" (7), and "to Anaṅgamadanā" (8). Outside of that are Brāhmī and the others. Outside of that are the Bhairavas:
"to Asitāṅgabhairava" (1), "to Rurubhairava" (2), "to Caṇḍabhairava" (3), and "to Krodhabhairava" (4).

One should worship on the tips of the petals with "Salutation to Unmāda-Bhairava," "5. Salutation to Kapāli-Bhairava," "7. Salutation to Bhīṣaṇa-Bhairava," and "8. Salutation to Saṃhāra-Bhairava. Then one should worship the world-protectors (lokapālas) in their respective directions. Thereafter, having offered the recitation according to one's capacity, one should perform the dismissal (visarjana). The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) consists of twelve hundred thousand [recitations] with [offerings] smeared with the three sweets (madhuratraya).

One should perform twelve thousand oblations with *palāśa* flowers; the oblation with *karavīra* flowers should be one-tenth of that amount. Through oblations of *palāśa* flowers, the practitioner of mantra attains perfection of speech.
One should prepare equal parts of camphor and *kapicora*; *jaṭāmāṃsī* should be four parts, and *rocanā* is considered to be the same amount.
Saffron should consist of seven parts, sandalwood is considered to be one part, and agarwood should be nine parts; such is the sequence of the proportions.
Having thoroughly purified all of that which has been ground by the maiden with snow-water,
one should take it and apply it as a tilaka; thus one shall make men lords of the earth.
Women, those intoxicated with the pride of youth and so forth, elephants maddened by rut,
lions, tigers, great serpents, bhūtas, vetālas, and rākṣasas—
A man who applies this *tilaka* brings others under his control merely by being seen. Now, the various divisions of its mantras:

1. *Īṃ*—this is one mantra. 2. *Aiṃ Rāṃ*—this is one mantra. 3. *Aiṃ Rī Kṣaṃ*—this is one mantra. 4. *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ*—this is one mantra. 5. *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Hauṃ*—this is one mantra. 6. *Saiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ*—this is one mantra. 7. *Śaiṃ Khlīṃ*... [and so forth].
Śrauṃ—this is one [syllable]. 7. Hraiṃ Hrīṃ Hrauṃ—this is one [syllable]. 8. Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauṃ. 9. Klīṃ Sauṃ Aiṃ. 10.
Śraiṃ Śrauṃ Śrīṃ. 11. Sakala Hrīṃ Saiṃ Haiṃ Saṃ. 12. Hrāṃ Sakala Hrīṃ. 13. Śrauṃ Śraiṃ Śrauṃ. 14. Sahaklīṃ Śraiṃ Śrūṃ Sklrīṃ Hrauṃ Sahaklauṃ. 15. Sahaiṃ Sahauṃ.

16. *hklīṃ* *sahaklīṃ* 17. *sahauṃ* *sahaklīṃ* 18. *śraiṃ* *sahaiṃ* *sahaklīṃ* 19. *sahaiṃ* *sahauṃ* *sahaiṃ* 20. *sahaklīṃ* *sahrauṃ* *sahaiṃ* 21. *sahrauṃ* *sahaklīṃ* *sahaiṃ* 22. *sahaiṃ* *aiṃ* *īṃ* *jauṃ* 23. *hasaiṃ* *hasaklīṃ* *hasauḥ* 24. *iṃ* *jauṃ* *aiṃ* 25. *jauṃ* *īṃ* *aiṃ* 26. Others than these.

There are other variations of this mantra, but they have not been written here due to the bulk of the text. For these, the rites from the invocation of the *ṛṣi* and others up to the worship are like those for Tripurā.

Now, the Bālatripurā mantra: *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*. Its *ṛṣi* is Dakṣiṇāmūrti, its *chandas* is Gāyatrī, its deity is Bālatripurā, *aiṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *klīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of knowledge. *Aiṃ*.
1. *klīṃ* on the two middle fingers; 2. *sauḥ* on the two ring fingers; 3. *aiṃ* on the two little fingers;
4. *aiṃ* on the two thumbs; 5. *klīṃ* on the two index fingers; 6. *sauḥ* on the palms; 7. *aiṃ* at the base (*ādhāra*); 8. *klīṃ* at the heart; 9.
*sauḥ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).

50b) One should perform the placement [of mantras] by pervading the body with *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*. *Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ sauḥ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ* (1). *Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ sauḥ hrīṃ śiraḥ* (2).

uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ sauḥ hrūṃ—[this is] the *śikhā* (crown lock) [mantra], thrice. eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ sauḥ hraiṃ—[this is] the *kavaca* (armor) [mantra], four times. oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ aṃ sauḥ hrauṃ—[this is for] the three eyes (*netratraya*), *vauṣaṭ*. aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaḥ aḥ sauḥ.

"Astrāya Phaṭ" (six times)—thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The meditation (*dhyāna*): Wearing earrings, armlets, jewels, necklaces, bracelets, and rings from which all impurities have been released; shining with bangles and other ornaments, with golden waist-bands and shimmering anklets; wearing a fine bodice of ruby-red hue like the bandhūka flower, she bears a digit of the moon.
[She holds] a noose, a goad, a book, and a rosary in her six right hands starting from the uppermost;
she has a serene face like the full moon, is illuminated by three eyes, and wears garments, garlands, and unguents shining white as the moon or milk. She has arisen from the *mūlādhāra*.

Meditating on the Blessed Lady within the lotus of the heart, one should exhale through the right nostril and cause her, stationed upon the flower, to enter the maṇḍala. Having thus meditated and worshipped her with mental offerings (mānasopacāra), one should begin the external worship:
"Oṃ guṃ aiṃ, salutation to the gurus beginning with Śiva; Oṃ aiṃ gaṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati"—thus [one worships] on the left and the right.

Having worshipped [the deity] in a vessel made of copper or other materials, provided with the *ādhāra* and so forth, upon the previously mentioned pedestal (*pīṭha*)— specifically within the nine-yoni mandala situated in the center of the eight petals— one should worship in the order of the corners starting from the east: *Aiṃ jayāyai namaḥ* (1), *Aiṃ vijayāyai* (2), *Aiṃ ajitāyai* (3).

One should worship with: *aiṃ* to Aparājitā (4), *aiṃ* to Nityā (5), *aiṃ* to Vilāsinī (6), *aiṃ* to Dogdhrī (7), *aiṃ* to Aghorā (8), *namaḥ*. One should worship Maṅgalā in the center with: *aiṃ maṃgalāyai namaḥ*. Therein, [one should worship] the previously mentioned...
Having invoked the Goddess, one should worship her with the services beginning with water for the feet (*pādya*). Then follows the worship of the limbs (*aṅga*) and the enclosures (*āvaraṇa*).

In the three triangles situated above—namely, the left-pointing and right-pointing triangles—one should worship with: "Aiṃ, obeisance to Rati" (1), "Klīṃ, obeisance to Prīti" (2), and "Sauḥ, obeisance to Manoramā" (3). One should worship the limbs in the southeast, northeast, southwest, northwest, in front, and behind. Drāṃ...

"Oṃ drāṃ, salutation to the arrow of liquefaction (drāvaṇa-vāṇa) 1; oṃ drīṃ, salutation to the arrow of delusion (mohana-vāṇa) 2"—with these, one should worship to the right of the Goddess. "Klīṃ, salutation to the arrow of torment (saṃtāpana-vāṇa)"—with this, one should worship behind her. "Klūṃ, salutation to the arrow of inflaming (saṃdīpana-vāṇa)"—with this, [one should worship] to the left. "Saḥ, salutation to the arrow of subjugation (vaśīkaraṇa-vāṇa)"—with this, [one should worship].

In front of the Goddess, one should worship Brāhmī and the others; thereafter, the world-protectors (lokapālas) should be worshipped. Having offered the recitation (japa), one should perform the dismissal (visarjana). The rest is like that of Bhairavī. "Klīṃ, O Goddess Tripurā, we know thee; O Kāmeśvarī, we meditate upon thee; may she, the Wet One (Klinnā), impel us"—this is the Gāyatrī of Tripurā, which brings about her presence.
In the ritual for Sarasvatī, one should offer cool fragrant flowers, as well as the auspicious sprouts of dūrvā grass and the rājavṛkṣa tree.
These shoots of the sindhuvāra plant are indeed praised;
however, one who constantly recites the Sarasvatī mantra should always avoid them.
The āmrāta, gṛñjana, viṅga, karañja, and likewise lasuna;
oil, palāṇḍu, piṇyāka, and even that which is with the thumb [i.e., the thumb-print mark] in one's food— [these are forbidden].
One who constantly seeks the grace of Sarasvatī must avoid all stale food;
he should not consume betel at night, nor should he approach a woman during the day.

One should never perform sexual intercourse during the two twilights, nor should one utter anything while impure; at the onset of night, one should observe silence and must not look upon a woman clad only in a garment of directions (naked).
A wise man should not approach a woman in her menses, nor should he revile a beautiful-eyed woman; he should not speak false words, nor should he step over a sacred book.
One who seeks the grace of Sarasvatī must not neglect or step over the leaves inscribed with syllables; such [precautions] and others like them must not be abandoned.
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Sārasvata Mantras," in the *Mantrakoṣa* compiled by the venerable Āśāditya Tripāṭhī.
Now, the glorious mantras.

Therein is the single-syllable mantra: *Śrīṃ*. For this *Śrī* mantra, Bhṛgu is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Trivṛt-Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Śrī is the deity (*devatā*), *Śaṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Īṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *Raṃ* is the peg (*kīlaka*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of great prosperity.
*Śrāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*—1. *Śrīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*—2. *Śrūṃ* to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*—3. *Śraiṃ*... [to the armor, *huṃ*]—4.

Hūṃ 4 for the armor; Śrauṃ Vauṣaṭ for the three eyes; Phaṭ for the weapon. The nyāsas taught in the Āgamas are now stated: Mahāśriye 1; Mahāvidyutprabhe Svāhā 2; Gaurī Mahābale Bandhabandha Svāhā 3; Dhṛti Svāhā 4; Huṃ Mahākāye Padmahaste Huṃ Phaṭ 5. Thus.

The five limbs. Then the meditation: May she, who possesses two lotuses, whose hands grant fearlessness and boons, who has the luster of molten gold, who is white, and who is being sprinkled with water from jars held by her two pairs of radiant arms; she whose crown is bound with a mass of jewels, and who wears most pure silken garments at her waist—may she [grant protection].

The lotus-eyed one, who is supreme and wealthy, whose navel is like a lotus, who makes the world full of aesthetic delight, and who is the abode of Lakṣmī as she rests upon a lotus—may he grant us prosperity.

Having meditated thus—[the deity] holding two lotuses with the upper right and left hands, and below them the gestures of fearlessness (*abhaya*) and boon (*vara*)—one should perform the external worship after the mental worship. One should worship the pedestal (*pīṭha*), beginning with the support (*ādhāra*). Aṃ...

Having worshipped in successive layers with "Salutation to Ādhāraśakti," 1. "to Mūlaprakṛti," 2. "to Maṇḍūka," 3. "to Kūrma," 4. "to Ananta," 5. "to Mahāvarāha," 6. "to Bhūmi," 7. "to Kṣīrodārṇava," 8. "to Śvetadvīpa," 9. "to Ratnamaṇḍapa," and 10. "to Ratnasiṃhāsana," [one should worship] the square pedestal (pīṭha) upon that.

Having visualized [the deities], one should worship them in the corners of the pedestal with the mantras: "Obeisance to Dharma," "Obeisance to Jñāna," "Obeisance to Vairāgya," and "Obeisance to Aiśvarya. One should worship on the sides of the pedestal with: "Obeisance to Adharma," "Obeisance to Ajñāna," "Obeisance to Avairāgya," and "Obeisance to Anaiśvarya. Then, [one should worship] with: "Obeisance to that Tamas," "Obeisance to the supreme Rajas," "Obeisance to Satva," and "Obeisance to Māṃ."

Having worshipped successively from top to bottom in the center of the seat with "Salutation to Māyā," "4," "to Vidyā," "5," "to the Fire-maṇḍala," "6," "to the Sun-maṇḍala," "7," and "Salutation to the Moon-maṇḍala," and having visualized a white lotus above that,
[one worships] with "Salutation to Vibhūti," "1," "to Unnati," "2," "to Kānti," "3," "to Hrī," "4," "to Kīrti," "5," "to Sannati," "6," and "to Puṣṭi," "7."
For the sake of excellence, one should worship on the petals with "Oṃ *yai* namaḥ.

Having invoked the Goddess into the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should worship her with the ritual services (*upacāra*) beginning with water for the feet (*pādya*). One should worship the limbs (*aṅga*) in the southeast, northeast, southwest, northwest, in front, and behind. [Then worship] Vāsudeva 1, Saṃkarṣaṇa 2, Pradyumna 3.

One should worship with "Salutation to Aniruddha" (4) in the primary directions starting from the east; and with "Salutation to Damaka" (1), "Salutation to Śalala" (2), "Salutation to Śulgulaka" (3), and "Salutation to Kuruṇṭaka" (4) on the petals at the corners. One should worship with "Salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi" on the right side.
Or, on the left side: "Homage to Padmanidhi. [And further: Homage to Valākī, Vimalā, Kamalā, Vanamaṇikā, Vibhīṣikā, Mālikā, Śāṅkarī, and Vasumālikā. Homage!

Thus, one should worship the eight [deities]. Having recited the mantra according to one's capacity and offered the oblation, one should dismiss [the deities]. The preparatory rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of thirty-two hundred thousand recitations. The fire sacrifice (*homa*) consists of twelve [thousand] oblations with lotuses or *vilva* wood fuel sticks smeared with the three sweets (*madhuratraya*). This brings about whatever one desires.
The practitioner, the best of adepts, by means of this ritual procedure, shall become enriched with wealth and grain;

he attains unassailable prosperity. One should recite this mantra at the measure of a chest [or for one's own benefit]. Restrained in mind, the practitioner, having meditated upon the Goddess within the solar orb, should recite this mantra three hundred thousand times.
The stable residence of Ramā may come to pass in a very short time. [This is] the mantra of Kamalavāsinī:

*namaḥ kamalavāsinyai svāhā*. For this [mantra], Dakṣa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Virāṭ is the meter (*chandas*), Kamalavāsinī is the deity (*devatā*), *nam* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and *svāhā* is the pinning-syllable (*kīlaka*) for the sake of attaining prosperity.

The Application (Viniyoga): Oṃ devyai namaḥ, to the heart; 1 Oṃ padminyai namaḥ, to the head; 2 Oṃ viṣṇupatnyai namaḥ, to the crest-lock (śikhā); 3 Oṃ varadāyai namaḥ, to the armor (kavaca); 4 [She who] dwells in the lotus, whose eyes are like lotuses, and who holds the lotus, the boon-granting gesture, and the pair of gestures of fearlessness... 5.
Illuminating the entire three worlds with the splendors of her body's radiant effulgence.
May she— whose jar-like breasts are lovely with pearl necklaces, who wears jeweled anklets,
and who holds a slow-moving mace and a jewel-encrusted crown— grant you auspiciousness; she who holds a lotus in her upper left hand and a boon-granting gesture (varada-mudrā) below it.

53a) Having invoked the Goddess into the sacred seat (pīṭha) mentioned in the *Śrīmantra*, one should worship her. Then, at the conclusion of the limb-worship (*aṅgapūjā*), one should worship Valākā and the others on the petals starting from the east, and the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) in their respective directions. [One should perform] ten lakhs [of recitations].

Puraścaraṇa: A fire sacrifice (homa) should be performed with lotuses mixed with the three sweets (trimadhu), using one-tenth the number [of recitations]. Now follows the Mahālakṣmī-hṛdaya-mantra, consisting of twenty-seven syllables in the form of a garland: Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kamale kamalālaye prasīda prasīda śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ mahālakṣmi namaḥ. [Salutation] to Mahālakṣmī.

In the *Śāradā-tilaka*, it is stated that "namaḥ" [is the mantra]. In some places, there are three seed-syllables (bījas) such as *śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ*; in others, two seed-syllables such as *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ*. For this [mantra], Dakṣa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), and Lakṣmī is the deity (*devatā*); its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of Lakṣmī. *Oṃ* is the seed-syllable, *śrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *hrīṃ* is the Praṇava.

The Kilaka. Then the five limbs: Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kamale śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, to the heart, namaḥ. 1 Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kamalālaye śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, to the head, svāhā. 2 Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ prasīda śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ. 3 Oṃ...

Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, be gracious! Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, for the armor, Huṃ 4. Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī! Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, for the weapon, Phaṭ 5. Meditation: [She who holds] a splendid vessel and a pair of lotuses in Her hands, a mirror, and is adorned with shimmering anklets, necklaces, armlets, pendants, bracelets, and a magnificent crown.

Trembling with her earrings, seated upon a lotus, attended by maidservants, and adorned with white unguents and garments— the Goddess Ramā, who destroys the sins of this day, became bowed down by divine hosts. Having meditated thus— [visualizing] two lotuses in the two upper hands,
a vessel of wealth in the lower right, and a mirror in the left— and having performed the mental worship:
One should worship the Goddess first in the Śrīpīṭha, from the foundation (ādhāra) up to the earth (bhūti).
(53b) Having performed the worship of the limbs (aṅgapūjā): Oṃ, salutation to Śrīdhara 1; to Hṛṣīkeśa 2; to Vaikuṇṭha 3.

One should worship with "Salutation to Viśvarūpa" (4) on the petals in the cardinal directions. One should worship with "Salutation to Vāsudeva (1), Saṃkarṣaṇa (2), Pradyumna (3), Aniruddha (4)" on the petals in the intermediate corners. One should worship with "Salutation to Bhāratī (1), Pārvatī (2), Cāndrī (3), Śacī (4)" on the petals in the cardinal directions. [And one should worship] Damaka (1), Salala (2), Gulgulu (3)...

"Salutation to Kuṇḍaka," four times—thus on the corner petals. "To Anurāga 1, Abhisaṃvāda 2, Vijaya 3, Vallabha 4, Mada 5, Bala 6, and Tejas 7, salutation!"—thus on the petals starting from the east. The worship and recitation of the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) are likewise in their respective directions. One hundred thousand recitations constitute the preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*).

An oblation of ten thousand bilva fruits smeared with the three sweets (madhuratraya) [should be performed]. Now, the Heart Mantra: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Jagatprasūtyai Namaḥ*. Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Mahālakṣmī is the deity (*devatā*); the application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of Lakṣmī. *Aiṃ* is the heart (1), *Hrīṃ* is the head (2).

*Śrīṃ* for the tuft (*śikhā*), *3* for the armor (*kavaca*), *klīṃ* for the armor (*kavaca*), *4* for the weapon (*astra*), *sauḥ* for the weapon (*astra*). With the entire mantra, perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*). One should place the five seed-syllables on the head, the chest, and from the genitals downwards. [The visualization (*dhyāna*)]: She possesses the luster of the rising sun, with a crown and necklace shining with crescent moons; she is adorned with jewel ornaments, her breasts are slightly bent, and she holds a cluster of blossoms in her hands.

One should meditate upon the Supreme Deity, who possesses three eyes like blooming lotuses, bears a radiant smile, and constantly holds two lotuses and the Kaustubha gem; in her two upper hands are two lotuses,
in her lower left hand is a sprout of the moon-plant (śaśinavallī), and in her lower right hand is the Kaustubha jewel.

Having meditated thus, accompanied by the ritual riches (*vibhūti*) and so forth, one should invoke and worship [the deity] seated upon a great jewel lion-throne beneath the *parijāta* tree on the pedestal (*pīṭha*), beginning with the support (*ādhāra*). Then follows the limb-enclosure (*aṅgāvaraṇa*) on the right side.

One should worship with "Salutation to Gaṇapati. On the left side, one should worship with "Salutation to Puṣpadhanvan. One should worship on the petals starting from the east with "Salutation to Umā," "Salutation to Śrī," "Salutation to Sarasvatī," "Salutation to Durgā," "Salutation to Dharaṇī," "Salutation to Gāyatrī," "Salutation to Devī," and "Salutation to Uṣā. Below the feet, one should worship with "Salutation to Gaṅgā" and "Salutation to Yamunā."

On both sides, one should worship with "Obeisance to Śaṅkhanidhi" and "Obeisance to Padmanidhi. To the west, [one should worship] with "Obeisance to Varuṇa, who holds a parasol in his hand. Around [the perimeter], one should worship the twelve *lagnas* (ascendants) with "Obeisance to Śeṣa.
Outside of that, one should worship the two planets with "Obeisance to Sūrya. In the eight directions, [one should worship] Airāvata... 1.

One should worship with the mantra: "Obeisance to Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Kumuda, Añjana, Puṣpadanta, Sārvabhauma, and Supratīka. Outside of that, one should worship Indra and the other [directional deities], and outside of those, their respective weapons. This is the ritual of worship. The preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations, [accompanied] by offerings of clarified butter.

One should perform ten thousand oblations (*homa*) with lotuses or wood-apples (*bilva*) individually. Standing in water reaching up to the neck and meditating on the Goddess within the sun, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times while extending both arms; thus one immediately attains health and certainly obtains wealth. One should daily offer one thousand and eight oblations of *śāli* rice, and before long—

Great prosperity is certainly produced. Now, the mantra for the four aims of life (caturvarga): it consists of four syllables: Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ. For this mantra, Bhṛgu is the seer (ṛṣi), and the meter is Tṛvṛdanuṣṭup. (54b)

The metre is Śrī; the goddess is Śrī; the seed-syllable (bīja) is *Śrīṃ*; the power (śakti) is *Īṃ*; the pin (kīlaka) is *Naṃ*; the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of great prosperity (*mahāsaṃpat*).
*Śrāṃ* is the heart (1); *Śrīṃ* is the head (2); *Śrūṃ* is the crest-lock (śikhā) (3); *Śraiṃ* is the armor (kavaca) (4);
*Śrauṃ* is the three eyes (netratraya) (5); *Śraḥ* is the weapon (astra) (6). Meditation (*dhyāna*): [She who possesses] a luster resembling rubies...

Having meditated thus—[the Goddess] who, with four lofty elephants resembling snow, their trunks playfully grasping jeweled pitchers, is being sprinkled [with water]; who holds in her right and left lower hands the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and in her upper hands a pair of lotuses; and who, out of longing for her beloved, holds a sprig of the *pārijāta* tree—I salute her, she who is seated upon a lotus. Then, having invoked the Goddess onto the previously mentioned pedestal:

One should perform worship. The preliminary rites (*āvaraṇa*) and so forth are as previously described. The preparatory rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations. An oblation (*homa*) of ten thousand red lotuses is performed. Now, another mantra: *Oṃ śuddhavyāsāya namaḥ mahāśriyai namaḥ*. The seer (*ṛṣi*) and other details are as before. *Oṃ* [is for] the heart. [The rest follows].

*Śuddhavāsase śirase svāhā* (2); *namaḥ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ* (3); *mahāśriyai kavacāya huṃ* (4); *namaḥ astrāya phaṭ* (5). The meditation, worship, and so forth are as previously described; the *puraścaraṇa* consists of three hundred thousand recitations. The fire sacrifice (*homa*) with lotuses is one-tenth of that amount. Now, another mantra: *Pautaumautabhayeśriye*.

Śrī Namaḥ. Jamadagni is the seer (ṛṣi) of this [mantra]; Triṣṭubh is the meter (chanda); Śrī is the deity (devatā). The application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of Lakṣmī. Pautaumautabhaye namaḥ—[this is] the heart (hṛdaya). 1. Pautaumautabhaye svāhā—[this is] the head (śiras). 2. Pautaumautabhaye—[this is] the crest-lock (śikhā). 3. Pautaumautabhaye—[this is] the armor (kavaca). 4. *Note: The term "stri*" in the source text appears to be a corruption of "tri-". **Note: The term "bhave" in the source text appears to be a corruption of "bhaye".**

*Namaḥ* is the armor (*kavaca*), [repeated] four times; *Śrīrnamaḥ* is the weapon (*astra*), [repeated] five times. The meditation, worship, and other rites are as previously described. One should recite twelve thousand [times] daily for seven nights. Thereupon, one becomes accomplished (*siddha*).
Having meditated upon the Goddess with a golden lotus in her hand at the three junctions of the day, one should mutter [the mantra] eight thousand times.

55a) One obtains one's desired object. By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one should apply a forehead mark (*tilaka*), collyrium, flowers, garments, and so forth; one will become the foremost among the illustrious. Likewise, by reciting it for three months, a village belongs to the Brahmin.

It is accomplished. Now follows the *Pradoma* mantra for casting [obstacles]: *Padmaprabhe padmasundari dharmarṣe svāhā*. Its seer (*ṛṣi*) and other attributes are as previously stated. *Padmaprabhe* is the heart (1); *padmasundari* is the head (2); *dharmarṣe* is the crest-lock (3); *svāhā* is the armor (4); and with the whole [mantra] is the weapon (5).

The previously mentioned recitation, worship, meditation, and so forth [should be performed]. One should remember the Vidyā—which has achieved its purpose through the methods of recitation and the like—as standing before the eyes of her angry husband. She becomes gracious and acts for him; she shall grant all desires like a wish-fulfilling creeper. Another mantra: *Namo brahmatanaye*.

The Ṛṣi and other [limbs] are as previously stated. "Obeisance to the son of Brahmā, obeisance to the heart," and so forth. Meditation, worship, and other rites are as before. Now, the Tripuṭā: *Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ*. *Hrīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *śrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *klīṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*). The application (*viniyoga*) is for the desired purpose. Having performed three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra.
Śrīṃ, the heart; 1. Hrīṃ, the head; 2. Klīṃ, the crest-lock; 3. Śrīṃ, the armor; 4. Hrīṃ, the three eyes;

5. Klīṃ, the weapon; 6. Meditation: Seated upon a lotus placed on a jeweled throne set within a grove of wish-fulfilling trees on a jeweled floor fashioned from ground as radiant as fresh gold; wearing a crown of bound jewels...
One should meditate upon her, who is adorned with jeweled earrings, shimmering armlets, a girdle, and a pair of anklets;
she holds a lotus, a pair of nooses, goads, and a bow, as well as flower-arrows, and possesses the color of fresh gold.

Behold her, who holds a chowrie, a mirror, a casket, and betel in her hands; who is surrounded by female attendants carrying fans; and who gazes at the practitioner with a gracious look. In her right and left secondary hands she holds two lotuses, below which are a noose and a goad, and below those, in her [primary] hands, a desired bow.

The two [deities] with flower-arrows (Puṣpabāṇau) are to be meditated upon. Having meditated thus, and having worshipped the pedestal (pīṭha) beginning with the Ādhāra and ending with Vibhūti, one should invoke the Goddess into the pericarp of the lotus situated there and worship her with the services (upacāras) such as water for the feet (pādya) and so forth. The limb-enclosure (aṅgāvaraṇa) is performed with the limbs (aṅgas). Then: 1. Lakṣmī, 2. Hari, 3. Gaurī, 4. Śiva, 5. Rati.

One should worship with "Salutation to Kāma" (6) in the corners of the hexagon. With "Salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi" and "Salutation to Padmanidhi," one should worship Brāhmī and the others on the eight petals at the two sides. One should also worship the world-protectors (lokapālas) in their respective directions.
The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) consists of twelve hundred thousand recitations, performed with fuel-sticks of the bilva tree or the ājaka tree.

One should perform twelve parts of the oblation with offerings smeared with the three sweets (trimadhu). Reciting the mantra of Śrī, the practitioner should also recite the Śrīsūktas. Desiring abundant prosperity, he should then become a speaker of truth.
Facing westward, he should eat his meals, speaking pleasant words preceded by a smile.

Restrained and pure, he should adorn himself with perfumes, flowers, and other ornaments; he should sleep on a comfortable bed with a young woman, and not otherwise. He should not descend into water naked, nor should he eat while anointed with oil.
One should not smear turmeric on the face, nor should one ever sleep while impure;
one should not scratch the ground in vain, nor [break] the bilva, the droṇa, or the lotus.
One should never wear salt or pure oil upon the head;
one should never become soiled with dirt, nor should one eat contemptible food.
One should never step over with one's feet the Droṇa, Paṅkaja, Vilva,
Sahādevī, Mṛdvīkā-vallī, Śrī-devī, or Viṣṇu-vallabhā plants.
One who is devoted to right conduct, a constant devotee of Viṣṇu, and firm in his vows, should always wear a *kanyā* flower and *jambū* sprouts upon his head.
One attains great glory, which is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
Now, the Śrīsūktas: O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī, who is golden-hued, tawny, adorned with garlands of gold and silver, and who is Indra’s golden sovereign. 1.
O Jātavedas, bring to me that fortune which never departs,
through which I may obtain gold, cattle, horses, and men.

With horses at its front, with a chariot in its midst, and delighting in the trumpeting of elephants—may the Goddess Śrī, the goddess of fortune, take pleasure in this dwelling; may the goddess Śrī favor me. 3.
I invoke Śrī, who is golden-hued, seated upon a lotus, possessing a golden enclosure, moist, blazing, satisfied, and bestowing satisfaction; she who is called Agnihotrā. || 4 ||
I take refuge in her who is moon-like, radiant, blazing with glory, the noble Śrī nourished by the gods in this world, the lotus-born one; may misfortune perish, for I choose you. || 5 ||
O you who possess the luster of the sun, born from austerity, this bilva tree is your forest-king;
may its fruits, through the power of austerity, dispel internal obstacles as well as external misfortune.
May the friend of the gods approach me, along with the fame of all living beings;
having manifested in this kingdom, may he grant me increasing renown. (7)
I destroy hunger, thirst, and the foremost of impurities; I drive away misfortune from the house, as well as lack of prosperity and all forms of failure.
I invoke here Śrī, who has the fragrance as her door, who is invincible, eternally nourished, the bestower of prosperity, and the sovereign of all beings.
May we obtain the desire of the mind and the intention; may we attain the truth of speech, the form of cattle, food, prosperity, and fame for our progeny. 10.
From Kardama, there was born a daughter named Saṃbhavakardamā;
and at the proper time, Śrī herself became his mother Ratnamālinī in the home.
May the waters release their moist essences in my house, which is free from distress;
may the goddess Jīvadēvī, the mother Śrī, dwell here in my family.
O Jātavedas, bring to me Lakṣmī— ārdrā, Puṣkariṇī, Puṣṭi, Piṅgalā, Hemamālinī, Candrā, Hiraṇmayī.
"O Jātavedas, bring me that fortune which does not depart;
in which there is abundant gold, cows, female slaves, luster, gifts to be given, and many men. (14)

One who desires prosperity, having become pure and self-restrained, should offer clarified butter daily; furthermore, one desiring prosperity should constantly recite the fifteen verses of the Śrīsūkta.
O lotus-faced one, O you who resemble a lotus, O lotus-eyed one, O you born from a lotus!
Since you favor me, O lotus-eyed one, may I obtain happiness.
O Goddess, bestower of horses, cows, and wealth, in this great abundance, may you cause wealth to flourish for us; O Giver of all desires, grant them to us.
May she, who is the mother of progeny, grant me sons, grandsons, wealth, grain, elephants, horses, cattle, and chariots,
and may she bring about my prosperity.
Agni is wealth, Vāyu is wealth, Sūrya is wealth, and Vasu is wealth;
Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Varuṇa are wealth—I release the bow for the sake of wealth.
May the slayer of Vṛtra drink the Soma being drunk by Vainateya;
may the possessor of Soma grant the wealth of Soma to the one who possesses Soma here.
Neither anger, nor envy, nor greed, nor an unwholesome mind arises in those who have performed meritorious deeds; such devotees should recite the Śrīsūkta.
It bestows glory, splendor, long life, health, freedom from humiliation, cattle, the birth of a son,
and a hundred-year lifespan of great longevity.
For this verse beginning with "hiraṇyavarṇā," Śrī is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ), and Śrī-Agni is the deity (devatā).
For the fourteen verses beginning with "tāṃ ma āvaha," the seers are the sons of Śrī, purified by the mud of bliss (ānandakardama-viklinna).

The meter (*chandaḥ*) of the two verses beginning with "tāṃ ma ā vahāśva pūrvām" is Anuṣṭubh; the meter of the verse beginning with "kāṃso'smi" is Prastārapaṅkti. For all [these verses], Agni is the deity (*devatā*); the first [letter] is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), the last is the power (*śakti*).
[This is for the attainment of Mahālakṣmī]. The application (*niyoga*) is as follows: [the letters are assigned to] the head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and neck.

One should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the fifteen verses in sequence upon the two arms, the heart, the navel, the genitals, the anus, the thighs, the knees, and the shanks. Having wiped both hands three times with the *praṇava* (OM), one should [place the mantras] from the thumb to the little finger, beginning with the *praṇava* and ending with the dative case, using the verse: "The golden one, with a garland of gold, with a garland of silver... and so forth.
Having placed [the syllables] ending in *namaḥ*, one should place those same [syllables] upon the heart and other [limbs]. Thereafter, one should meditate upon the Supreme Goddess.

May the Mother of the World— whose form during meditation possesses the color and appearance of a mass of pollen from a dawn lotus, who holds a lotus and displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness with her two hands, and who is adorned with a jeweled crown and a multitude of various ornaments— be present.

Having meditated thus—[Śrī] is continuous, with two lotuses upon her hands and the gestures of boon (*vara*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*) below them—one should invoke Śrī upon the pedestal described in the Śrī-mantra and worship her. The invocation is performed with the verse beginning "hiraṇyavarṇām" (1);
having prepared the seat with the verse beginning "tāṃ ma āvaha" (2), one offers the *argha* with the verse beginning "aśvapūrvām" (3).

With the verse "kāṃsosmi," the water for washing the feet is offered; with "caṃdrām," the water for sipping (ācamanīya); with "ādityavarṇā," the honey-mixture (madhuparka); with "upaitu mām," the ceremonial bath (abhiṣeka); with "kṣutpipāsām," the garment; with "gaṃdhadvārām," the ornaments; and with "manasaḥ kāmam," the unguent.
One should fashion the flowers with this [verse] beginning with *kardamena* (11). Then, one should worship the retinue. Then, on the petals:

one should worship with "Salutation to Padmā" (1), "Salutation to Padmavarṇā" (2), "to Padmasthā" (3), "to Ārdā" (4), "to Tarpayantī" (5), "to Tṛptā" (6), "to Jvalinī" (7), and "Salutation to Svarṇaprakārā" (8). And [one should worship] the world-protectors (*lokapālas*).
In their respective directions; outside of those, their weapons. Then: "Obeisance to the Blessed Lady together with her retinue.
With the mantra *āpaḥ sṛjantu*, offer incense (12); with the mantra *ārdāṃ puṣkariṇī nityam*, offer a lamp (13);
with the mantra *ārdām*, offer the food offering (14). Then, having performed the auspicious *rātrika* rite for the Goddess, [place] it in the fire.
Having offered one oblation each with ghee and food, having provided water for rinsing the mouth (ācamanīya) to the Goddess, and having praised her,
one should cause the Goddess to enter one's own heart with the verse beginning "tām ma āvaha.

Thus ends the worship. Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight until the eleventh day, one who is devoted to celibacy, observing silence, and wearing white garments and ornaments, should perform twelve thousand recitations. On the twelfth day, [one should offer] lotuses smeared with the three sweets (*trimadhu*), fuel-sticks of the *bilva* tree, milk-rice (*pāyasa*), and ghee.
One should offer oblations three hundred times with each [mantra]. One should feed twelve Brahmins. The mantra becomes perfected. It is as follows:
"In the rite of bathing, one should always sprinkle water three times over with those hymns."
Facing the sun, one should recite the mantra and likewise offer libations with water.

During forty Thursdays of practice, having recited the final verse one hundred and eight times, one should offer lotuses smeared with fresh butter in that same number. By means of this very [verse], "I am Kāṃsa," great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*) arises within six months. Every day, at the conclusion of the libation (*tarpaṇa*), one should also satisfy [the deities] with these [offerings]. Oṃ.
I offer libations to Śrī (1), Lakṣmī (2), Varadā (3), Viṣṇupatnī (4), Vasudā (5),
Hiraṇyarūpā (6), Suvarṇamālinī (7), Rajatasrajā (8), Suvarṇagṛhā (9), Suvarṇaprākārā (10), Padmavāsinī (11), Padmahastā (12), and Padmapriyā (13).

To Muktālaṅkārā (14), to Sūryā (15), to Candrā (16), to Vilvapriyā (17), to Īśvarā (18), to Bhukti (19), to Pramukti (20), to Vibhūti (21), to Ṛddhi (22), to Samṛddhi (23), to Tuṣṭi (24), to Puṣṭi (25), to Dhanadā (26), to Dhaneśvarī (27), to Śraddhā (28), to Bhoginī (29), and to Bhogadā.
"Obeisance to Dhātrī and Vidhātrī"— this is the ritual procedure for the *sūkta*.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Mantras of Lakṣmī," in the *Mantrakoṣa* compiled by the venerable Āśāditya Tripāṭhī.
58b) Now, the mantras of Āditya: therein, for the daily worship (nityapūjā), having bathed in due order beginning with Sadyojāta and so forth, and having put on two clean garments,
one should thereafter perform the rites of the twilight prayers (saṃdhyā) and so on, and approach the vicinity of the worship pavilion (pūjāmaṇḍapa).

Having performed the purification of the feet and the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), [one should say]: "Obeisance to you, Yamabhairava, who possesses an exceedingly fierce and massive body like the fire at the end of an aeon;

you ought to grant me permission. "Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Kṣaṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla. Having thus bowed to the right side, and then to the left, [one bows] to the Goddess of the Door (Dvāraśrī).

"Salutation! [he says]. "Salutation to the threshold of the door," he says at the threshold. Then, uttering the weapon-mantra, "Phaṭ! To the Weapon," while contracting his left side and entering with the tip of his left foot first, scattering mustard seeds, he should expel the obstructors with a fierce gaze.

"May those beings who have departed and those beings established on earth, who are the doers of harm, perish by the command of Śiva! Oṃ astrāya phaṭ! Homage to the seat!"—thus the seat is worshipped. Having sat there, the articles of worship are placed to the right and [the water vessels] to the left.

Having mentally conceived the offerings such as the sacrificial altar (vedī) and so forth, and having performed three rounds of breath control (prāṇāyāma) with the root mantra, one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), the installation of the vital breath (prāṇapratiṣṭhā), and the nyāsa of the Mātṛkās according to the previously mentioned method.
However, this is not to be done for every individual worship; such is the general rule. Now, the fourfold [rite] of the Sun...

For this mantra: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), Savitṛ is the deity (devatā); "I" is the seed-syllable (bīja), "saḥ" is the power (śakti), and the Praṇava is the pin (kīlaka). Some say "oṃ" is the seed-syllable and "hrīṃ" is the power.
Its application (viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining desired goals such as health and so forth. Oṃ, salutation to the heart (1).
59a) *Hrīṃ* to the head, svāhā; 2. *Oṃ* to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ; 3. *Oṃ hrīṃ* to the armor, huṃ; 4.
*Oṃ* to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ; 5. *Oṃ hrīṃ* to the weapon, phaṭ. Having thus performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), [one should perform] meditation (*dhyāna*).

One should perform [the worship] of Him who, with the luster of the moon shimmering upon His crown of radiant jewels, instantly surpasses their beautiful splendors— splendors as brilliant as molten gold,

lotuses, and hibiscus flowers— with His own radiance; and who, with His non-cold [cool] hands, sets ablaze the entire expanse of the sky by means of the noose, goad, wish-granting jewel, and the gesture of fearlessness.

May the right breast of the Mother of the World, lofty with its folds, protect you; may her right and left upper hands hold a noose and a goad, while below them, in her two lower hands, the gestures of granting boons (*varada*) and fearlessness (*abhaya*) are to be meditated upon. Having thus meditated and worshipped her with offerings of food (*naivedya*) and mental services (*mānasa-upacāra*), one should begin the external worship (*bāhyapūjā*). *Gaṃ gurubhyo namaḥ*.
Having remembered "Oṃ Gaṇapataye Namaḥ" on both sides, one should then place the arghya vessel in front.

Having drawn a triangle on the ground, worship it with: "Oṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala, whose self consists of the ten dharmakalās. Then, having placed a conch or other vessel upon its base, [worship] the sun-maṇḍala.

Having worshipped the vessel with "Obeisance to the one whose self consists of twelve digits" (12), 2; having poured water therein with the root mantra and worshipped the water with "Obeisance to the lunar orb, whose self consists of sixteen nectar-digits" (3);
and having thrown flowers, sandalwood, and so forth therein, consecrated it as nectar (*amṛtīkṛtya*), and displayed the cow-seal (*dhenumudrā*).
Covering [the vessel] with both hands, one should recite either the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) or the *rāṣṭraka* mantra. One should worship on the left side, saying: "Obeisance to the Gurus;

obeisance to the Supreme Gurus (*paramaguru*); obeisance to the Higher-Lower Gurus (*parāparaguru*). On the right side, one should worship, saying: "Obeisance to Gaṇapati. Now follows the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*). In the deity-vessel, [one worships] the Support Power (*ādhāraśakti*).
Salutations: 1. to Mūlaprakṛti, 2. to Maṇḍuka, 3. to Kūrma, 4. to Kālāgnirudra, 5.
to Ananta, 6. to Varāha, 7. to Bhūmi, 8. to Nāla, 9. to Kamala—salutations, thus [one offers] higher and higher.

Having worshipped [the deity] and envisioned a square pedestal (*pīṭha*) above it, one should worship in the corners starting from the southeast with: "Obeisance to Prabhūtā," "Obeisance to Vimalā," "Obeisance to Sārasā," and "Obeisance to Samārādhyā. In the center, [one should worship] with: "Obeisance to Paramasukhā. In those same corners, [one should worship] with: "Obeisance to Dharma," "Obeisance to Jñāna," "Obeisance to Vairāgya," and "Obeisance to Aiśvarya."

Thus one should worship. In the principal directions starting from the east, one should worship with: "Obeisance to Adharma," "Obeisance to Ignorance," "Obeisance to Non-detachment," and "Obeisance to Non-sovereignty. Then: "Taṃ, obeisance to Tamas"; "Raṃ, obeisance to Rajas"; "Saṃ, obeisance to Sattva"; "Māṃ, obeisance to Māyā"; "Viṃ, obeisance to Vidyā"; "Ātmane"; "Antarātmane"; "Paramātmane."

Having worshipped in succession from above— saying "Salutation to the Fire-maṇḍala whose essence is knowledge" (9), "to the Sun-maṇḍala" (10), and "to the Moon-maṇḍala" (11)— one should visualize an eight-petaled lotus above that and worship on the petals starting from the east with:
*rāṃ* to Dīptā (1), *rīṃ* to Sūkṣmā (2), *rūṃ* to Jayā (3), *reṃ* to Bhadrā (4), *raiṃ*...

One should worship with: "Oṃ *Vibhūtyai* [namaḥ]," 5. "*Rauṃ Vimalāyai*," 6. "*Riṃ Amṛtāyai*," 7. "*Raṃ Vidyutāyai namaḥ*. In the center, one should worship with: "*Raḥ Sarvatomukhyai namaḥ*. Having worshipped the pedestal (*pīṭha*) with: "*Namaḥ to the Sun-god, whose essence is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, and who is the self of the yoga-pedestal*," one should invoke the deity there. [This is] the invocation.

Having displayed the mudrās of *sthāpana* (establishing), *svārāta* (self-restraint), *saṃnirodha* (confinement), *avaguṇṭhana* (veiling), and *saṃvyāyana* (clothing), one should perform everything with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). Then, having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) upon the body of the deity, [one offers] water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), the arghya offering, water for sipping, the honey-mixture (*madhuparka*), water for sipping, water for bathing and sipping, clothing, fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and the waving of lights (*ārātrika*).

One should offer incense, lamps, and food offerings with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). Then, one should worship the front, the back, and the limbs in the directions of Agni, Īśāna, Asura, and Vāyu. [One should worship] Hṛllekhā (1), Gaganā (2), Raktā (3), Karālikā (4), and Mahocchuṣmā (5) with "Namaḥ" in the five directions starting from the east. [And] Soma (1) in the north-east.
Salutation to Aṅgāraka (Mars) here;
salutation to Budha (Mercury), Śanaiścara (Saturn), Vṛhaspati (Jupiter), Rāhu, Śukra (Venus), and Ketu.

Thus one should worship. And [one should worship] the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) in their respective directions. Having worshipped thus, one should offer the *prasannārgha* (the propitiatory offering). It is as follows: while reciting the mantra in reverse order, one should pour water into the *argha* vessel and cast into it *kuśa* grass, flowers, *dūrvā* grass, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), sandalwood paste, sesame seeds, mustard seeds, and barley. Then, one should offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) to the deity.

Having offered the *argha* vessel, lifted it with both hands, and recited the root mantra one hundred and eight times, he should kneel upon the ground, bring the vessel to his forehead, and offer the *argha*. Then, having recited the mantra according to his capacity and made the offering, he should withdraw [the deity] into his heart. Thus, having performed the worship.
Let the floral remains (nirmālya) and the sacred fire (tejas) be given to Caṇḍa. The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) consists of four hundred thousand recitations.

The oblation (homa), performed with Kiṃśuka flowers or lotuses, should be one-twelfth of that number. For the autumnal [rite], the materials for the respectful offering (arghya) are those prescribed for the Tilaka rite.
Saffron, gorocanā, nāgakeśara, red sandalwood, bamboo,
karavīra, japā, śāli rice, kuśa grass, and grains of śyāmāka.
Having cast [the water] into that ocean through the sun of one's resolve,
this offering of *argha* bestows longevity, health, and prosperity.
It bestows wealth, grain, cattle, fields, sons, friends, and a wife;
it grants splendor, heroism, fame, renown, learning, prosperity, and good fortune.
Thus one should recite this on every Sunday.

Now, the *tilaka* for the purpose [of the mantra]: *hrīṃ hrīṃ saḥ*. For this [mantra], Brahmā is the *ṛṣi*, Gāyatrī is the *chandas*, Sūrya is the deity, *hrāṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *saḥ* is the power (*śakti*), *hrīṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of one's desired goal.
One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) starting from the secret place up to the feet with *hrāṃ*; and starting from the throat up to the secret place with *hrīṃ*.
2. One should place [the mantras] beginning from the head and ending at the throat. 3. Hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ (1);
Hrīṃ śiraḥ (2); Hrūṃ śikhā (3); Hraiṃ kavacaṃ (4); Hrauṃ netratrayaṃ (5); Hraḥ astraṃ (6).
Meditation: May the Sun protect you—he who holds a pair of large, ruddy lotuses as red as the morning sun;
